AI.conclusion: Foundation models like MedSAM can be successfully adapted for multi-class medical image segmentation with minimal architectural changes. The approach shows promise for extending to more diverse medical imaging scenarios in future work, potentially reducing the need for task-specific adjustments required by traditional methods.

title: Biomimetic PINNs for Cell-Induced Phase Transitions: UQ-R3 Sampling with Causal Gating
summary: Nonconvex multi-well energies in cell-induced phase transitions give rise to sharp interfaces, fine-scale microstructures, and distance-dependent inter-cell coupling, all of which pose significant challenges for physics-informed learning. Existing methods often suffer from over-smoothing in near-field patterns. To address this, we propose biomimetic physics-informed neural networks (Bio-PINNs), a variational framework that encodes temporal causality into explicit spatial causality via a progressive distance gate. Furthermore, Bio-PINNs leverage a deformation-uncertainty proxy for the interfacial length scale to target microstructure-prone regions, providing a computationally efficient alternative to explicit second-derivative regularization. We provide theoretical guarantees for the resulting uncertainty-driven ``retain-resample-release" adaptive collocation strategy, which ensures persistent coverage under gating and establishing a quantitative near-to-far growth bound. Across single- and multi-cell benchmarks, diverse separations, and various regularization regimes, Bio-PINNs consistently recover sharp transition layers and tether morphologies, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art adaptive and ungated baselines.

AI.tldr: Bio-PINNs: A biomimetic physics-informed neural network framework that addresses over-smoothing in cell-induced phase transitions by encoding temporal causality into spatial causality via progressive distance gates and using deformation-uncertainty proxies for adaptive collocation.
AI.motivation: Nonconvex multi-well energies in cell-induced phase transitions create sharp interfaces, fine-scale microstructures, and distance-dependent inter-cell coupling, posing significant challenges for physics-informed learning. Existing methods suffer from over-smoothing in near-field patterns, failing to capture the intricate microstructural features essential for accurate modeling of these complex biological phenomena.
AI.method: Bio-PINNs use a variational framework that encodes temporal causality into explicit spatial causality through a progressive distance gate. They leverage a deformation-uncertainty proxy for interfacial length scale to target microstructure-prone regions, providing efficient alternative to explicit second-derivative regularization. The method employs an uncertainty-driven "retain-resample-release" adaptive collocation strategy with theoretical guarantees for persistent coverage under gating and quantitative near-to-far growth bounds.
AI.result: Bio-PINNs consistently recover sharp transition layers and tether morphologies across single- and multi-cell benchmarks, diverse separations, and various regularization regimes. They significantly outperform state-of-the-art adaptive and ungated baselines, demonstrating superior capability in capturing the complex microstructural features of cell-induced phase transitions.
AI.conclusion: The Bio-PINNs framework successfully addresses the over-smoothing problem in physics-informed learning for cell-induced phase transitions by introducing biomimetic principles, progressive distance gating, and uncertainty-driven adaptive collocation. The method provides both theoretical guarantees and practical performance improvements for modeling complex biological systems with sharp interfaces and fine-scale microstructures.

title: Authorship Impersonation via LLM Prompting does not Evade Authorship Verification Methods
summary: Authorship verification (AV), the task of determining whether a questioned text was written by a specific individual, is a critical part of forensic linguistics. While manual authorial impersonation by perpetrators has long been a recognized threat in historical forensic cases, recent advances in large language models (LLMs) raise new challenges, as adversaries may exploit these tools to impersonate another's writing. This study investigates whether prompted LLMs can generate convincing authorial impersonations and whether such outputs can evade existing forensic AV systems. Using GPT-4o as the adversary model, we generated impersonation texts under four prompting conditions across three genres: emails, text messages, and social media posts. We then evaluated these outputs against both non-neural AV methods (n-gram tracing, Ranking-Based Impostors Method, LambdaG) and neural approaches (AdHominem, LUAR, STAR) within a likelihood-ratio framework. Results show that LLM-generated texts failed to sufficiently replicate authorial individuality to bypass established AV systems. We also observed that some methods achieved even higher accuracy when rejecting impersonation texts compared to genuine negative samples. Overall, these findings indicate that, despite the accessibility of LLMs, current AV systems remain robust against entry-level impersonation attempts across multiple genres. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this counter-intuitive resilience stems, at least in part, from the higher lexical diversity and entropy inherent in LLM-generated texts.

AI.tldr: LLM-generated authorial impersonations fail to bypass established forensic authorship verification systems, with some methods performing better against impersonations than genuine negative samples.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether prompted LLMs can generate convincing authorial impersonations that evade existing forensic authorship verification systems, addressing new challenges posed by LLM accessibility for adversarial impersonation.
AI.method: Used GPT-4o to generate impersonation texts under four prompting conditions across three genres (emails, text messages, social media posts), then evaluated against both non-neural (n-gram tracing, Ranking-Based Impostors Method, LambdaG) and neural (AdHominem, LUAR, STAR) AV methods within a likelihood-ratio framework.
AI.result: LLM-generated texts failed to sufficiently replicate authorial individuality to bypass established AV systems; some methods achieved higher accuracy when rejecting impersonation texts compared to genuine negative samples.
AI.conclusion: Current AV systems remain robust against entry-level LLM impersonation attempts across multiple genres, with resilience partly stemming from higher lexical diversity and entropy in LLM-generated texts.

title: Hierarchical Visual Relocalization with Nearest View Synthesis from Feature Gaussian Splatting
summary: Visual relocalization is a fundamental task in the field of 3D computer vision, estimating a camera's pose when it revisits a previously known scene. While point-based hierarchical relocalization methods have shown strong scalability and efficiency, they are often limited by sparse image observations and weak feature matching. In this work, we propose SplatHLoc, a novel hierarchical visual relocalization framework that uses Feature Gaussian Splatting as the scene representation. To address the sparsity of database images, we propose an adaptive viewpoint retrieval method that synthesizes virtual candidates with viewpoints more closely aligned with the query, thereby improving the accuracy of initial pose estimation. For feature matching, we observe that Gaussian-rendered features and those extracted directly from images exhibit different strengths across the two-stage matching process: the former performs better in the coarse stage, while the latter proves more effective in the fine stage. Therefore, we introduce a hybrid feature matching strategy, enabling more accurate and efficient pose estimation. Extensive experiments on both indoor and outdoor datasets show that SplatHLoc enhances the robustness of visual relocalization, setting a new state-of-the-art.

AI.tldr: SplatHLoc: A hierarchical visual relocalization framework using Feature Gaussian Splatting as scene representation, with adaptive viewpoint retrieval and hybrid feature matching for improved accuracy and robustness.
AI.motivation: Point-based hierarchical relocalization methods are limited by sparse image observations and weak feature matching, which hinders their effectiveness in camera pose estimation when revisiting known scenes.
AI.method: Uses Feature Gaussian Splatting as scene representation; proposes adaptive viewpoint retrieval to synthesize virtual candidates aligned with query viewpoints; introduces hybrid feature matching combining Gaussian-rendered features (better for coarse stage) and directly extracted image features (better for fine stage).
AI.result: Extensive experiments on indoor and outdoor datasets show SplatHLoc enhances robustness of visual relocalization and sets new state-of-the-art performance.
AI.conclusion: SplatHLoc effectively addresses limitations of point-based methods through novel scene representation and hybrid matching strategy, achieving superior visual relocalization performance.

title: Improving Ensemble Forecasts of Abnormally Deflecting Tropical Cyclones with Fused Atmosphere-Ocean-Terrain Data
summary: Deep learning-based tropical cyclone (TC) forecasting methods have demonstrated significant potential and application advantages, as they feature much lower computational cost and faster operation speed than numerical weather prediction models. However, existing deep learning methods still have key limitations: they can only process a single type of sequential trajectory data or homogeneous meteorological variables, and fail to achieve accurate forecasting of abnormal deflected TCs. To address these challenges, we present two groundbreaking contributions. First, we have constructed a multimodal and multi-source dataset named AOT-TCs for TC forecasting in the Northwest Pacific basin. As the first dataset of its kind, it innovatively integrates heterogeneous variables from the atmosphere, ocean, and land, thus obtaining a comprehensive and information-rich meteorological dataset. Second, based on the AOT-TCs dataset, we propose a forecasting model that can handle both normal and abnormally deflected TCs. This is the first TC forecasting model to adopt an explicit atmosphere-ocean-terrain coupling architecture, enabling it to effectively capture complex interactions across physical domains. Extensive experiments on all TC cases in the Northwest Pacific from 2017 to 2024 show that our model achieves state-of-the-art performance in TC forecasting: it not only significantly improves the forecasting accuracy of normal TCs but also breaks through the technical bottleneck in forecasting abnormally deflected TCs.

AI.tldr: AOT-TCs dataset and model for tropical cyclone forecasting that integrates atmosphere-ocean-terrain data and handles both normal and abnormal deflected TCs in the Northwest Pacific basin.
AI.motivation: Existing deep learning methods for TC forecasting have limitations: they only process single-type sequential trajectory data or homogeneous meteorological variables, and fail to accurately forecast abnormal deflected TCs. Current approaches lack comprehensive multimodal integration of heterogeneous variables from different physical domains.
AI.method: Two main contributions: 1) Construction of AOT-TCs dataset - a multimodal, multi-source dataset integrating heterogeneous variables from atmosphere, ocean, and land for TC forecasting in the Northwest Pacific basin. 2) Development of a forecasting model with explicit atmosphere-ocean-terrain coupling architecture that can handle both normal and abnormally deflected TCs.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on all TC cases in the Northwest Pacific from 2017-2024 show state-of-the-art performance: significant improvement in forecasting accuracy for normal TCs and breakthrough in forecasting abnormally deflected TCs, which was previously a technical bottleneck.
AI.conclusion: The proposed AOT-TCs dataset and explicit atmosphere-ocean-terrain coupling model represent groundbreaking contributions that overcome key limitations of existing deep learning methods for TC forecasting, enabling comprehensive multimodal integration and accurate prediction of both normal and abnormal TC behavior.

title: M-MiniGPT4: Multilingual VLLM Alignment via Translated Data
comment: 6 pages, ACL 2026, Proceedings of the 7th Workshop on African Natural Language Processing (AfricaNLP 2026)
summary: This paper presents a Multilingual Vision Large Language Model, named M-MiniGPT4. Our model exhibits strong vision-language understanding (VLU) capabilities across 11 languages. We utilize a mixture of native multilingual and translated data to push the multilingual VLU performance of the MiniGPT4 architecture. In addition, we propose a multilingual alignment training stage that uses parallel text corpora to further enhance the multilingual capabilities of our model. M-MiniGPT4 achieves 36% accuracy on the multilingual MMMU benchmark, outperforming state-of-the-art models in the same weight class, including foundation models released after the majority of this work was completed. We open-source our models, code, and translated datasets to facilitate future research in low-resource and multilingual settings.

AI.tldr: M-MiniGPT4 is a multilingual vision-language model that achieves strong performance across 11 languages using mixed native/translated data and parallel text alignment, outperforming SOTA models in its weight class.
AI.motivation: To develop a multilingual vision-language understanding model that performs well across multiple languages, addressing the need for cross-lingual capabilities in vision-language tasks and improving performance in low-resource language settings.
AI.method: 1) Uses MiniGPT4 architecture as base; 2) Employs mixture of native multilingual and translated data for training; 3) Introduces multilingual alignment training stage using parallel text corpora to enhance cross-lingual capabilities.
AI.result: Achieves 36% accuracy on multilingual MMMU benchmark, outperforming state-of-the-art models in same weight class, including foundation models released after most of this work was completed.
AI.conclusion: M-MiniGPT4 demonstrates strong multilingual vision-language understanding across 11 languages, with released models, code, and translated datasets to support future research in multilingual and low-resource settings.

title: SLVMEval: Synthetic Meta Evaluation Benchmark for Text-to-Long Video Generation
summary: This paper proposes the synthetic long-video meta-evaluation (SLVMEval), a benchmark for meta-evaluating text-to-video (T2V) evaluation systems. The proposed SLVMEval benchmark focuses on assessing these systems on videos of up to 10,486 s (approximately 3 h). The benchmark targets a fundamental requirement, namely, whether the systems can accurately assess video quality in settings that are easy for humans to assess. We adopt a pairwise comparison-based meta-evaluation framework. Building on dense video-captioning datasets, we synthetically degrade source videos to create controlled "high-quality versus low-quality" pairs across 10 distinct aspects. Then, we employ crowdsourcing to filter and retain only those pairs in which the degradation is clearly perceptible, thereby establishing an effective final testbed. Using this testbed, we assess the reliability of existing evaluation systems in ranking these pairs. Experimental results demonstrate that human evaluators can identify the better long video with 84.7%-96.8% accuracy, and in nine of the 10 aspects, the accuracy of these systems falls short of human assessment, revealing weaknesses in text-to-long-video evaluation.

AI.tldr: SLVMEval is a benchmark for meta-evaluating text-to-video evaluation systems on long videos (up to 3 hours), testing their ability to accurately assess video quality in human-perceptible degradation scenarios.
AI.motivation: Current text-to-video evaluation systems lack proper assessment on long videos, and there's a need to determine if these systems can accurately evaluate video quality in scenarios that are easily perceptible to humans.
AI.method: The authors create a synthetic long-video meta-evaluation benchmark using dense video-captioning datasets. They synthetically degrade source videos to create controlled "high-quality vs low-quality" pairs across 10 distinct aspects, then use crowdsourcing to filter pairs where degradation is clearly perceptible, establishing a final testbed for pairwise comparison-based meta-evaluation.
AI.result: Human evaluators achieve 84.7%-96.8% accuracy in identifying better long videos. In 9 out of 10 aspects, existing evaluation systems perform worse than human assessment, revealing significant weaknesses in text-to-long-video evaluation.
AI.conclusion: The SLVMEval benchmark exposes limitations in current text-to-video evaluation systems for long videos, demonstrating that these systems fall short of human-level performance in most quality assessment aspects, highlighting the need for improved evaluation methodologies for long-form video content.

title: Derived Fields Preserve Fine-Scale Detail in Budgeted Neural Simulators
summary: Fine-scale-faithful neural simulation under fixed storage budgets remains challenging. Many existing methods reduce high-frequency error by improving architectures, training objectives, or rollout strategies. However, under budgeted coarsen-quantize-decode pipelines, fine detail can already be lost when the carried state is constructed. In the canonical periodic incompressible Navier-Stokes setting, we show that primitive and derived fields undergo systematically different retained-band distortions under the same operator. Motivated by this observation, we formulate Derived-Field Optimization (DerivOpt), a general state-design framework that chooses which physical fields are carried and how storage budget is allocated across them under a calibrated channel model. Across the full time-dependent forward subset of PDEBench, DerivOpt not only improves pooled mean rollout nRMSE, but also delivers a decisive advantage in fine-scale fidelity over a broad set of strong baselines. More importantly, the gains are already visible at input time, before rollout learning begins. This indicates that the carried state is often the dominant bottleneck under tight storage budgets. These results suggest a broader conclusion: in budgeted neural simulation, carried-state design should be treated as a first-class design axis alongside architecture, loss, and rollout strategy.

AI.tldr: DerivOpt improves fine-scale fidelity in neural PDE simulation by optimizing which physical fields to carry and how to allocate storage budget across them, addressing state construction as a primary bottleneck under fixed storage constraints.
AI.motivation: Fine-scale-faithful neural simulation under fixed storage budgets is challenging because existing methods focus on architectures, training objectives, or rollout strategies, while fine detail can be lost during state construction in budgeted coarsen-quantize-decode pipelines.
AI.method: Derived-Field Optimization (DerivOpt) - a state-design framework that chooses which physical fields to carry and how to allocate storage budget across them under a calibrated channel model, based on the observation that primitive and derived fields undergo systematically different retained-band distortions under the same operator.
AI.result: Across the full time-dependent forward subset of PDEBench, DerivOpt improves pooled mean rollout nRMSE and delivers decisive advantage in fine-scale fidelity over strong baselines. Gains are visible at input time before rollout learning begins, indicating carried state is often the dominant bottleneck under tight storage budgets.
AI.conclusion: Carried-state design should be treated as a first-class design axis alongside architecture, loss, and rollout strategy in budgeted neural simulation.

title: Calibrated Confidence Expression for Radiology Report Generation
summary: Safe deployment of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) in radiology report generation requires not only accurate predictions but also clinically interpretable indicators of when outputs should be thoroughly reviewed, enabling selective radiologist verification and reducing the risk of hallucinated findings influencing clinical decisions. One intuitive approach to this is verbalized confidence, where the model explicitly states its certainty. However, current state-of-the-art language models are often overconfident, and research on calibration in multimodal settings such as radiology report generation is limited. To address this gap, we introduce ConRad (Confidence Calibration for Radiology Reports), a reinforcement learning framework for fine-tuning medical LVLMs to produce calibrated verbalized confidence estimates alongside radiology reports. We study two settings: a single report-level confidence score and a sentence-level variant assigning a confidence to each claim. Both are trained using the GRPO algorithm with reward functions based on the logarithmic scoring rule, which incentivizes truthful self-assessment by penalizing miscalibration and guarantees optimal calibration under reward maximization. Experimentally, ConRad substantially improves calibration and outperforms competing methods. In a clinical evaluation we show that ConRad's report level scores are well aligned with clinicians' judgment. By highlighting full reports or low-confidence statements for targeted review, ConRad can support safer clinical integration of AI-assistance for report generation.

AI.tldr: ConRad: A reinforcement learning framework for calibrating verbalized confidence estimates in radiology report generation to enable selective radiologist verification and reduce hallucination risks.
AI.motivation: Safe deployment of LVLMs in radiology requires clinically interpretable confidence indicators to enable selective verification and reduce risks from hallucinated findings influencing clinical decisions. Current models are often overconfident, and calibration research in multimodal radiology settings is limited.
AI.method: ConRad uses reinforcement learning (GRPO algorithm) to fine-tune medical LVLMs for calibrated verbalized confidence estimates. Two settings: report-level confidence scores and sentence-level confidence for each claim. Reward functions based on logarithmic scoring rule penalize miscalibration and guarantee optimal calibration under reward maximization.
AI.result: ConRad substantially improves calibration and outperforms competing methods. Clinical evaluation shows ConRad's report-level scores align well with clinicians' judgment. The framework enables highlighting full reports or low-confidence statements for targeted review.
AI.conclusion: ConRad supports safer clinical integration of AI-assisted radiology report generation by providing calibrated confidence estimates that enable selective radiologist verification, reducing risks from hallucinated findings influencing clinical decisions.

title: 3D Architect: An Automated Approach to Three-Dimensional Modeling
summary: The aim of our paper is to render an object in 3-dimension using a set of its orthographic views. Corner detector (Harris Detector) is applied on the input views to obtain control points. These control points are projected perpendicular to respective views, in order to construct an envelope. A set of points describing the object in 3-dimension, are obtained from the intersection of these mutually perpendicular envelopes. These set of points are used to regenerate the surfaces of the object using computational geometry. At the end, the object in 3-dimension is rendered using OpenGL

AI.tldr: 3D object reconstruction from orthographic views using Harris corner detection, envelope intersection, and computational geometry with OpenGL rendering.
AI.motivation: To develop a method for reconstructing 3D objects from 2D orthographic views, which is useful in CAD, engineering design, and computer graphics applications where 3D models need to be generated from traditional 2D engineering drawings.
AI.method: 1. Apply Harris corner detector on input orthographic views to obtain control points. 2. Project control points perpendicular to respective views to construct 3D envelopes. 3. Compute intersection points of mutually perpendicular envelopes to obtain 3D point cloud. 4. Use computational geometry techniques to regenerate surfaces from the 3D points. 5. Render final 3D object using OpenGL.
AI.result: Successfully reconstructs 3D objects from orthographic views by converting 2D corner features into 3D points through envelope intersection, then generating surfaces for visualization.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method effectively reconstructs 3D objects from orthographic views using corner detection and geometric intersection techniques, providing a practical approach for converting traditional 2D engineering drawings into 3D models.

title: Robust and Consistent Ski Rental with Distributional Advice
summary:
The ski rental problem is a canonical model for online decision-making under uncertainty, capturing the fundamental trade-off between repeated rental costs and a one-time purchase. While classical algorithms focus on worst-case competitive ratios and recent "learning-augmented" methods leverage point-estimate predictions, neither approach fully exploits the richness of full distributional predictions while maintaining rigorous robustness guarantees. We address this gap by establishing a systematic framework that integrates distributional advice of unknown quality into both deterministic and randomized algorithms.
  For the deterministic setting, we formalize the problem under perfect distributional prediction and derive an efficient algorithm to compute the optimal threshold-buy day. We provide a rigorous performance analysis, identifying sufficient conditions on the predicted distribution under which the expected competitive ratio (ECR) matches the classic optimal randomized bound. To handle imperfect predictions, we propose the Clamp Policy, which restricts the buying threshold to a safe range controlled by a tunable parameter. We show that this policy is both robust, maintaining good performance even with large prediction errors, and consistent, approaching the optimal performance as predictions become accurate.
  For the randomized setting, we characterize the stopping distribution via a Water-Filling Algorithm, which optimizes expected cost while strictly satisfying robustness constraints. Experimental results across diverse distributions (Gaussian, geometric, and bi-modal) demonstrate that our framework improves consistency significantly over existing point-prediction baselines while maintaining comparable robustness.

AI.tldr: A framework for ski rental problem that integrates full distributional predictions (not just point estimates) into both deterministic and randomized algorithms, with rigorous robustness guarantees and improved consistency.
AI.motivation: Classical ski rental algorithms focus on worst-case competitive ratios, while recent learning-augmented methods use point-estimate predictions. Neither fully exploits rich distributional predictions while maintaining robustness guarantees.
AI.method: For deterministic setting: formalize problem under perfect distributional prediction, derive optimal threshold-buy day algorithm, propose Clamp Policy with tunable parameter for imperfect predictions. For randomized setting: characterize stopping distribution via Water-Filling Algorithm that optimizes expected cost while satisfying robustness constraints.
AI.result: Identifies sufficient conditions where expected competitive ratio matches classic optimal randomized bound. Clamp Policy is robust to prediction errors and consistent with accurate predictions. Water-Filling Algorithm maintains robustness while optimizing expected cost. Experiments show significant consistency improvements over point-prediction baselines across Gaussian, geometric, and bi-modal distributions.
AI.conclusion: The framework successfully integrates distributional advice into ski rental algorithms, achieving better consistency than point-prediction methods while maintaining comparable robustness, bridging the gap between classical worst-case analysis and learning-augmented approaches.

title: MemFactory: Unified Inference & Training Framework for Agent Memory
summary: Memory-augmented Large Language Models (LLMs) are essential for developing capable, long-term AI agents. Recently, applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to optimize memory operations, such as extraction, updating, and retrieval, has emerged as a highly promising research direction. However, existing implementations remain highly fragmented and task-specific, lacking a unified infrastructure to streamline the integration, training, and evaluation of these complex pipelines. To address this gap, we present MemFactory, the first unified, highly modular training and inference framework specifically designed for memory-augmented agents. Inspired by the success of unified fine-tuning frameworks like LLaMA-Factory, MemFactory abstracts the memory lifecycle into atomic, plug-and-play components, enabling researchers to seamlessly construct custom memory agents via a "Lego-like" architecture. Furthermore, the framework natively integrates Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to fine-tune internal memory management policies driven by multi-dimensional environmental rewards. MemFactory provides out-of-the-box support for recent cutting-edge paradigms, including Memory-R1, RMM, and MemAgent. We empirically validate MemFactory on the open-source MemAgent architecture using its publicly available training and evaluation data. Across both in-domain and out-of-distribution evaluation sets, MemFactory consistently improves performance over the corresponding base models, with relative gains of up to 14.8%. By providing a standardized, extensible, and easy-to-use infrastructure, MemFactory significantly lowers the barrier to entry, paving the way for future innovations in memory-driven AI agents.

AI.tldr: MemFactory is a unified framework for training and evaluating memory-augmented LLM agents, featuring modular memory lifecycle components and integrated GRPO optimization.
AI.motivation: Existing RL-based memory optimization approaches for LLMs are fragmented and task-specific, lacking a unified infrastructure for integrating, training, and evaluating complex memory agent pipelines.
AI.method: MemFactory abstracts memory lifecycle into atomic plug-and-play components with Lego-like architecture, integrates Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) for fine-tuning memory management policies, and supports cutting-edge paradigms like Memory-R1, RMM, and MemAgent.
AI.result: Empirical validation on MemAgent architecture shows consistent performance improvements over base models across in-domain and out-of-distribution evaluations, with relative gains up to 14.8%.
AI.conclusion: MemFactory provides standardized, extensible infrastructure that lowers entry barriers and enables future innovations in memory-driven AI agents.

title: Developing Adaptive Context Compression Techniques for Large Language Models (LLMs) in Long-Running Interactions
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) often experience performance degradation during long-running interactions due to increasing context length, memory saturation, and computational overhead. This paper presents an adaptive context compression framework that integrates importance-aware memory selection, coherence-sensitive filtering, and dynamic budget allocation to retain essential conversational information while controlling context growth. The approach is evaluated on LOCOMO, LOCCO, and LongBench benchmarks to assess answer quality, retrieval accuracy, coherence preservation, and efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves consistent improvements in conversational stability and retrieval performance while reducing token usage and inference latency compared with existing memory and compression-based approaches. These findings indicate that adaptive context compression provides an effective balance between long-term memory preservation and computational efficiency in persistent LLM interactions

AI.tldr: Adaptive context compression framework for LLMs improves long-running interaction performance by selectively retaining essential information while controlling context growth.
AI.motivation: LLMs suffer performance degradation in long-running interactions due to increasing context length, memory saturation, and computational overhead, necessitating efficient context management.
AI.method: Adaptive context compression framework integrating importance-aware memory selection, coherence-sensitive filtering, and dynamic budget allocation to retain essential conversational information.
AI.result: Consistent improvements in conversational stability and retrieval performance while reducing token usage and inference latency on LOCOMO, LOCCO, and LongBench benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Adaptive context compression effectively balances long-term memory preservation and computational efficiency in persistent LLM interactions.

title: Stochastic Dimension Implicit Functional Projections for Exact Integral Conservation in High-Dimensional PINNs
summary: Enforcing exact macroscopic conservation laws, such as mass and energy, in neural partial differential equation (PDE) solvers is computationally challenging in high dimensions. Traditional discrete projections rely on deterministic quadrature that scales poorly and restricts mesh-free formulations like PINNs. Furthermore, high-order operators incur heavy memory overhead, and generic optimization often lacks convergence guarantees for non-convex conservation manifolds. To address this, we propose the Stochastic Dimension Implicit Functional Projection (SDIFP) framework. Instead of projecting discrete vectors, SDIFP applies a global affine transformation to the continuous network output. This yields closed-form solutions for integral constraints via detached Monte Carlo (MC) quadrature, bypassing spatial grid dependencies. For scalable training, we introduce a doubly-stochastic unbiased gradient estimator (DS-UGE). By decoupling spatial sampling from differential operator subsampling, the DS-UGE reduces memory complexity from $\mathcal{O}(M \times N_{\mathcal{L}})$ to $\mathcal{O}(N \times |\mathcal{I}|)$. SDIFP mitigates sampling variance, preserves solution regularity, and maintains $\mathcal{O}(1)$ inference efficiency, providing a scalable, mesh-free approach for solving conservative high-dimensional PDEs.

AI.tldr: SDIFP is a framework for enforcing exact macroscopic conservation laws in neural PDE solvers using stochastic dimension implicit functional projection with doubly-stochastic unbiased gradient estimation for scalable, mesh-free high-dimensional PDE solving.
AI.motivation: Traditional methods for enforcing exact macroscopic conservation laws (mass, energy) in neural PDE solvers face computational challenges: discrete projections rely on deterministic quadrature that scales poorly in high dimensions, restrict mesh-free formulations like PINNs, incur heavy memory overhead from high-order operators, and generic optimization lacks convergence guarantees for non-convex conservation manifolds.
AI.method: Proposes Stochastic Dimension Implicit Functional Projection (SDIFP) framework that applies global affine transformation to continuous network output instead of projecting discrete vectors, yielding closed-form solutions for integral constraints via detached Monte Carlo quadrature. Introduces doubly-stochastic unbiased gradient estimator (DS-UGE) that decouples spatial sampling from differential operator subsampling to reduce memory complexity from O(M × N_ℒ) to O(N × |ℐ|).
AI.result: SDIFP bypasses spatial grid dependencies, mitigates sampling variance, preserves solution regularity, maintains O(1) inference efficiency, and provides a scalable, mesh-free approach for solving conservative high-dimensional PDEs with exact macroscopic conservation law enforcement.
AI.conclusion: SDIFP offers a computationally efficient framework for enforcing exact conservation laws in neural PDE solvers, addressing scalability limitations of traditional methods while supporting mesh-free formulations and providing convergence guarantees through stochastic optimization techniques.

title: Distilling Human-Aligned Privacy Sensitivity Assessment from Large Language Models
comment: Accepted to the LREC CALD-pseudo 2026 Workshop
summary: Accurate privacy evaluation of textual data remains a critical challenge in privacy-preserving natural language processing. Recent work has shown that large language models (LLMs) can serve as reliable privacy evaluators, achieving strong agreement with human judgments; however, their computational cost and impracticality for processing sensitive data at scale limit real-world deployment. We address this gap by distilling the privacy assessment capabilities of Mistral Large 3 (675B) into lightweight encoder models with as few as 150M parameters. Leveraging a large-scale dataset of privacy-annotated texts spanning 10 diverse domains, we train efficient classifiers that preserve strong agreement with human annotations while dramatically reducing computational requirements. We validate our approach on human-annotated test data and demonstrate its practical utility as an evaluation metric for de-identification systems.

AI.tldr: Distilling privacy assessment capabilities from large LLMs into lightweight encoder models for efficient privacy evaluation of textual data
AI.motivation: Accurate privacy evaluation of textual data is critical but challenging; while LLMs can serve as reliable privacy evaluators, their computational cost and impracticality for processing sensitive data at scale limit real-world deployment.
AI.method: Distill privacy assessment capabilities from Mistral Large 3 (675B) into lightweight encoder models (as few as 150M parameters) using a large-scale dataset of privacy-annotated texts spanning 10 diverse domains, training efficient classifiers that preserve strong agreement with human annotations.
AI.result: Lightweight models achieve strong agreement with human annotations while dramatically reducing computational requirements; validated on human-annotated test data and demonstrated practical utility as an evaluation metric for de-identification systems.
AI.conclusion: The approach successfully addresses the gap between accurate privacy evaluation and computational practicality by distilling LLM capabilities into efficient models suitable for real-world deployment in privacy-preserving NLP applications.

title: Multi-Layered Memory Architectures for LLM Agents: An Experimental Evaluation of Long-Term Context Retention
summary: Long-horizon dialogue systems suffer from semanticdrift and unstable memory retention across extended sessions. This paper presents a Multi-Layer Memory Framework that decomposes dialogue history into working, episodic, and semantic layers with adaptive retrieval gating and retention regularization. The architecture controls cross-session drift while maintaining bounded context growth and computational efficiency. Experiments on LOCOMO, LOCCO, and LoCoMo show improved performance, achieving 46.85 Success Rate, 0.618 overall F1 with 0.594 multi-hop F1, and 56.90% six-period retention while reducing false memory rate to 5.1% and context usage to 58.40%. Results confirm enhanced long-term retention and reasoning stability under constrained context budgets.

AI.tldr: Multi-Layer Memory Framework for long-horizon dialogue systems addresses semantic drift and memory retention issues through layered memory decomposition with adaptive retrieval and retention regularization.
AI.motivation: Long-horizon dialogue systems suffer from semantic drift and unstable memory retention across extended sessions, requiring better memory management to maintain coherence and reasoning stability.
AI.method: Proposes a Multi-Layer Memory Framework that decomposes dialogue history into working, episodic, and semantic layers with adaptive retrieval gating and retention regularization to control cross-session drift while maintaining bounded context growth.
AI.result: Achieved 46.85 Success Rate, 0.618 overall F1 with 0.594 multi-hop F1, 56.90% six-period retention while reducing false memory rate to 5.1% and context usage to 58.40% on LOCOMO, LOCCO, and LoCoMo benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: The framework enhances long-term retention and reasoning stability under constrained context budgets, confirming effectiveness in mitigating semantic drift and improving memory management in extended dialogue sessions.

title: Monodense Deep Neural Model for Determining Item Price Elasticity
comment: Accepted at AAIML 2026 (International Conference on Advances in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning). Copyright 2026 IEEE. 6 pages, 4 figures
summary:
Item Price Elasticity is used to quantify the responsiveness of consumer demand to changes in item prices, enabling businesses to create pricing strategies and optimize revenue management. Sectors such as store retail, e-commerce, and consumer goods rely on elasticity information derived from historical sales and pricing data. This elasticity provides an understanding of purchasing behavior across different items, consumer discount sensitivity, and demand elastic departments. This information is particularly valuable for competitive markets and resource-constrained businesses decision making which aims to maximize profitability and market share. Price elasticity also uncovers historical shifts in consumer responsiveness over time. In this paper, we model item-level price elasticity using large-scale transactional datasets, by proposing a novel elasticity estimation framework which has the capability to work in an absence of treatment control setting. We test this framework by using Machine learning based algorithms listed below, including our newly proposed Monodense deep neural network.
  (1) Monodense-DL network -- Hybrid neural network architecture combining embedding, dense, and Monodense layers (2) DML -- Double machine learning setting using regression models (3) LGBM -- Light Gradient Boosting Model
  We evaluate our model on multi-category retail data spanning millions of transactions using a back testing framework. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of our proposed neural network model within the framework compared to other prevalent ML based methods listed above.

AI.tldr: Proposes a novel machine learning framework for estimating item-level price elasticity from transactional data without requiring treatment-control settings, with a Monodense-DL neural network outperforming other ML methods.
AI.motivation: Businesses need accurate price elasticity estimates to optimize pricing strategies and revenue management, but traditional methods often require controlled experimental settings that are impractical in real-world retail environments.
AI.method: A novel elasticity estimation framework that works without treatment-control settings, using three ML approaches: (1) Monodense-DL network (hybrid neural network with embedding, dense, and Monodense layers), (2) Double Machine Learning (DML) with regression models, and (3) Light Gradient Boosting Model (LGBM).
AI.result: Experimental evaluation on multi-category retail data with millions of transactions shows the proposed Monodense-DL neural network outperforms DML and LGBM methods in elasticity estimation accuracy.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework enables practical price elasticity estimation from observational data, with the Monodense-DL architecture providing superior performance for revenue optimization and pricing strategy development.

title: LLM Probe: Evaluating LLMs for Low-Resource Languages
summary: Despite rapid advances in large language models (LLMs), their linguistic abilities in low-resource and morphologically rich languages are still not well understood due to limited annotated resources and the absence of standardized evaluation frameworks. This paper presents LLM Probe, a lexicon-based assessment framework designed to systematically evaluate the linguistic skills of LLMs in low-resource language environments. The framework analyzes models across four areas of language understanding: lexical alignment, part-of-speech recognition, morphosyntactic probing, and translation accuracy. To illustrate the framework, we create a manually annotated benchmark dataset using a low-resource Semitic language as a case study. The dataset comprises bilingual lexicons with linguistic annotations, including part-of-speech tags, grammatical gender, and morphosyntactic features, which demonstrate high inter-annotator agreement to ensure reliable annotations. We test a variety of models, including causal language models and sequence-to-sequence architectures. The results reveal notable differences in performance across various linguistic tasks: sequence-to-sequence models generally excel in morphosyntactic analysis and translation quality, whereas causal models demonstrate strong performance in lexical alignment but exhibit weaker translation accuracy. Our results emphasize the need for linguistically grounded evaluation to better understand LLM limitations in low-resource settings. We release LLM Probe and the accompanying benchmark dataset as open-source tools to promote reproducible benchmarking and to support the development of more inclusive multilingual language technologies.

AI.tldr: LLM Probe is a lexicon-based framework for systematically evaluating LLMs' linguistic abilities in low-resource languages, tested on a Semitic language case study revealing performance differences between model types.
AI.motivation: Limited understanding of LLMs' linguistic capabilities in low-resource and morphologically rich languages due to scarce annotated resources and lack of standardized evaluation frameworks.
AI.method: Developed LLM Probe framework with four evaluation areas: lexical alignment, part-of-speech recognition, morphosyntactic probing, and translation accuracy. Created manually annotated benchmark dataset for a low-resource Semitic language with bilingual lexicons and linguistic annotations.
AI.result: Sequence-to-sequence models excel in morphosyntactic analysis and translation quality, while causal models perform well in lexical alignment but show weaker translation accuracy. Framework reveals notable performance differences across linguistic tasks.
AI.conclusion: Linguistically grounded evaluation is essential for understanding LLM limitations in low-resource settings. The open-source release of LLM Probe and benchmark dataset aims to promote reproducible benchmarking and support inclusive multilingual language technologies.

title: LightHarmony3D: Harmonizing Illumination and Shadows for Object Insertion in 3D Gaussian Splatting
summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables high-fidelity reconstruction of scene geometry and appearance. Building on this capability, inserting external mesh objects into reconstructed 3DGS scenes enables interactive editing and content augmentation for immersive applications such as AR/VR, virtual staging, and digital content creation. However, achieving physically consistent lighting and shadows for mesh insertion remains challenging, as it requires accurate scene illumination estimation and multi-view consistent rendering. To address this challenge, we present LightHarmony3D, a novel framework for illumination-consistent mesh insertion in 3DGS scenes. Central to our approach is our proposed generative module that predicts a full 360° HDR environment map at the insertion location via a single forward pass. By leveraging generative priors instead of iterative optimization, our method efficiently captures dominant scene illumination and enables physically grounded shading and shadows for inserted meshes while maintaining multi-view coherence. Furthermore, we introduce the first dedicated benchmark for mesh insertion in 3DGS, providing a standardized evaluation framework for assessing lighting consistency and photorealism. Extensive experiments across multiple real-world reconstruction datasets demonstrate that LightHarmony3D achieves state-of-the-art realism and multi-view consistency.

AI.tldr: LightHarmony3D enables physically consistent lighting and shadows for mesh insertion in 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes using a generative module to predict HDR environment maps.
AI.motivation: While 3DGS enables high-fidelity scene reconstruction, inserting external mesh objects with physically consistent lighting and shadows remains challenging for AR/VR, virtual staging, and digital content creation applications.
AI.method: Proposes a generative module that predicts a full 360° HDR environment map at insertion locations via single forward pass, leveraging generative priors instead of iterative optimization for efficient illumination capture and physically grounded shading.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art realism and multi-view consistency across multiple real-world reconstruction datasets, with the framework also introducing the first dedicated benchmark for mesh insertion in 3DGS.
AI.conclusion: LightHarmony3D provides an effective solution for illumination-consistent mesh insertion in 3DGS scenes, enabling physically consistent lighting and shadows while maintaining multi-view coherence for immersive applications.

title: Lie Generator Networks for Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations
summary: Linear dynamical systems are fully characterized by their eigenspectra, accessible directly from the generator of the dynamics. For nonlinear systems governed by partial differential equations, no equivalent theory exists. We introduce Lie Generator Network--Koopman (LGN-KM), a neural operator that lifts nonlinear dynamics into a linear latent space and learns the continuous-time Koopman generator ($L_k$) through a decomposition $L_k = S - D_k$, where $S$ is skew-symmetric representing conservative inter-modal coupling, and $D_k$ is a positive-definite diagonal encoding modal dissipation. This architectural decomposition enforces stability and enables interpretability through direct spectral access to the learned dynamics. On two-dimensional Navier--Stokes turbulence, the generator recovers the known dissipation scaling and a complete multi-branch dispersion relation from trajectory data alone with no physics supervision. Independently trained models at different flow regimes recover matched gauge-invariant spectral structure, exposing a gauge freedom in the Koopman lifting. Because the generator is provably stable, it enables guaranteed long-horizon stability, continuous-time evaluation at arbitrary time, and physics-informed cross-viscosity model transfer.

AI.tldr: LGN-KM is a neural operator that learns continuous-time Koopman generators for nonlinear PDEs through a stable decomposition (skew-symmetric + positive-definite diagonal), enabling interpretable spectral analysis and guaranteed stability.
AI.motivation: For nonlinear systems governed by PDEs, there's no equivalent to the eigenspectrum theory available for linear dynamical systems. The authors aim to develop a framework that can lift nonlinear dynamics into a linear latent space while maintaining interpretability and stability guarantees.
AI.method: Lie Generator Network--Koopman (LGN-KM) learns the continuous-time Koopman generator L_k through a decomposition L_k = S - D_k, where S is skew-symmetric (conservative inter-modal coupling) and D_k is positive-definite diagonal (modal dissipation). This architectural decomposition enforces stability and enables direct spectral access.
AI.result: On 2D Navier-Stokes turbulence, the generator recovers known dissipation scaling and complete multi-branch dispersion relation from trajectory data alone. Independently trained models at different flow regimes recover matched gauge-invariant spectral structure, exposing gauge freedom in Koopman lifting. The provably stable generator enables guaranteed long-horizon stability, continuous-time evaluation at arbitrary time, and physics-informed cross-viscosity model transfer.
AI.conclusion: LGN-KM provides a neural operator framework that bridges the gap between linear and nonlinear dynamical systems by learning interpretable Koopman generators with stability guarantees, enabling spectral analysis of nonlinear PDEs and facilitating cross-regime model transfer.

title: Impact of enriched meaning representations for language generation in dialogue tasks: A comprehensive exploration of the relevance of tasks, corpora and metrics
summary: Conversational systems should generate diverse language forms to interact fluently and accurately with users. In this context, Natural Language Generation (NLG) engines convert Meaning Representations (MRs) into sentences, directly influencing user perception. These MRs usually encode the communicative function (e.g., inform, request, confirm) via DAs and enumerate the semantic content with slot-value pairs. In this work, our objective is to analyse whether providing a task demonstrator to the generator enhances the generations of a fine-tuned model. This demonstrator is an MR-sentence pair extracted from the original dataset that enriches the input at training and inference time. The analysis involves five metrics that focus on different linguistic aspects, and four datasets that differ in multiple features, such as domain, size, lexicon, MR variability, and acquisition process. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study on dialogue NLG implementing a comparative analysis of the impact of MRs on generation quality across domains, corpus characteristics, and the metrics used to evaluate these generations. Our key insight is that the proposed enriched inputs are effective for complex tasks and small datasets with high variability in MRs and sentences. They are also beneficial in zero-shot settings for any domain. Moreover, the analysis of the metrics shows that semantic metrics capture generation quality more accurately than lexical metrics. In addition, among these semantic metrics, those trained with human ratings can detect omissions and other subtle semantic issues that embedding-based metrics often miss. Finally, the evolution of the metric scores and the excellent results for Slot Accuracy and Dialogue Act Accuracy demonstrate that the generative models present fast adaptability to different tasks and robustness at semantic and communicative intention levels.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes whether providing task demonstrators (MR-sentence pairs) to NLG models improves generation quality across diverse datasets, finding benefits for complex tasks, small datasets, and zero-shot settings.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether enriching NLG model inputs with task demonstrators (MR-sentence pairs from the dataset) enhances generation quality, particularly across different domains, dataset characteristics, and evaluation metrics.
AI.method: Used fine-tuned NLG models with enriched inputs containing MR-sentence demonstrator pairs. Conducted comparative analysis across four diverse datasets varying in domain, size, lexicon, MR variability, and acquisition process. Evaluated using five metrics focusing on different linguistic aspects.
AI.result: Enriched inputs are effective for complex tasks and small datasets with high MR/sentence variability, beneficial in zero-shot settings across domains. Semantic metrics (especially those trained with human ratings) capture generation quality more accurately than lexical metrics. Models show fast adaptability to tasks and robustness at semantic/communicative intention levels.
AI.conclusion: Task demonstrators improve NLG generation quality, particularly for challenging scenarios. Semantic evaluation metrics are superior to lexical ones, with human-trained metrics detecting subtle semantic issues. The approach enables robust adaptation to diverse tasks.

title: CCDNet: Learning to Detect Camouflage against Distractors in Infrared Small Target Detection
summary: Infrared target detection (IRSTD) tasks have critical applications in areas like wilderness rescue and maritime search. However, detecting infrared targets is challenging due to their low contrast and tendency to blend into complex backgrounds, effectively camouflaging themselves. Additionally, other objects with similar features (distractors) can cause false alarms, further degrading detection performance. To address these issues, we propose a novel \textbf{C}amouflage-aware \textbf{C}ounter-\textbf{D}istraction \textbf{Net}work (CCDNet) in this paper. We design a backbone with Weighted Multi-branch Perceptrons (WMPs), which aggregates self-conditioned multi-level features to accurately represent the target and background. Based on these rich features, we then propose a novel Aggregation-and-Refinement Fusion Neck (ARFN) to refine structures/semantics from shallow/deep features maps, and bidirectionally reconstruct the relations between the targets and the backgrounds, highlighting the targets while suppressing the complex backgrounds to improve detection accuracy. Furthermore, we present a new Contrastive-aided Distractor Discriminator (CaDD), enforcing adaptive similarity computation both locally and globally between the real targets and the backgrounds to more precisely discriminate distractors, so as to reduce the false alarm rate. Extensive experiments on infrared image datasets confirm that CCDNet outperforms other state-of-the-art methods.

AI.tldr: CCDNet is a novel infrared target detection network that addresses camouflage and distractor challenges through weighted multi-branch perceptrons, aggregation-refinement fusion, and contrastive distractor discrimination.
AI.motivation: Infrared target detection faces challenges due to low contrast, target camouflage in complex backgrounds, and false alarms from distractors with similar features, requiring improved detection accuracy and reduced false alarm rates.
AI.method: Proposes CCDNet with three key components: 1) Weighted Multi-branch Perceptrons (WMPs) backbone for multi-level feature aggregation, 2) Aggregation-and-Refinement Fusion Neck (ARFN) for bidirectional target-background relation reconstruction, and 3) Contrastive-aided Distractor Discriminator (CaDD) for adaptive similarity computation to distinguish real targets from distractors.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on infrared image datasets demonstrate that CCDNet outperforms other state-of-the-art methods in detection accuracy and false alarm reduction.
AI.conclusion: CCDNet effectively addresses infrared target detection challenges by combining feature aggregation, target-background relation modeling, and distractor discrimination, achieving superior performance for applications like wilderness rescue and maritime search.

title: From Physics to Surrogate Intelligence: A Unified Electro-Thermo-Optimization Framework for TSV Networks
comment: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems (IEEE TCAD)
summary: High-density through-substrate vias (TSVs) enable 2.5D/3D heterogeneous integration but introduce significant signal-integrity and thermal-reliability challenges due to electrical coupling, insertion loss, and self-heating. Conventional full-wave finite-element method (FEM) simulations provide high accuracy but become computationally prohibitive for large design-space exploration. This work presents a scalable electro-thermal modeling and optimization framework that combines physics-informed analytical modeling, graph neural network (GNN) surrogates, and full-wave sign-off validation. A multi-conductor analytical model computes broadband S-parameters and effective anisotropic thermal conductivities of TSV arrays, achieving $5\%-10\%$ relative Frobenius error (RFE) across array sizes up to $15x15$. A physics-informed GNN surrogate (TSV-PhGNN), trained on analytical data and fine-tuned with HFSS simulations, generalizes to larger arrays with RFE below $2\%$ and nearly constant variance. The surrogate is integrated into a multi-objective Pareto optimization framework targeting reflection coefficient, insertion loss, worst-case crosstalk (NEXT/FEXT), and effective thermal conductivity. Millions of TSV configurations can be explored within minutes, enabling exhaustive layout and geometric optimization that would be infeasible using FEM alone. Final designs are validated with Ansys HFSS and Mechanical, showing strong agreement. The proposed framework enables rapid electro-thermal co-design of TSV arrays while reducing per-design evaluation time by more than six orders of magnitude.

AI.tldr: A scalable electro-thermal modeling and optimization framework for TSV arrays using physics-informed analytical models and GNN surrogates, achieving 6 orders of magnitude speedup for design exploration.
AI.motivation: High-density TSVs enable 2.5D/3D heterogeneous integration but create signal-integrity and thermal-reliability challenges. Conventional FEM simulations are computationally prohibitive for large design-space exploration.
AI.method: Combines physics-informed analytical modeling, graph neural network (GNN) surrogates, and full-wave validation. Multi-conductor analytical model computes S-parameters and thermal conductivities. TSV-PhGNN surrogate trained on analytical data and fine-tuned with HFSS simulations.
AI.result: Analytical model achieves 5-10% RFE for arrays up to 15x15. GNN surrogate generalizes to larger arrays with RFE below 2%. Framework enables millions of TSV configurations to be explored within minutes with 6 orders of magnitude speedup.
AI.conclusion: The framework enables rapid electro-thermal co-design of TSV arrays, making exhaustive layout and geometric optimization feasible while maintaining accuracy through physics-informed modeling and surrogate techniques.

title: Baby Scale: Investigating Models Trained on Individual Children's Language Input
summary: Modern language models (LMs) must be trained on many orders of magnitude more words of training data than human children receive before they begin to produce useful behavior. Assessing the nature and origins of this "data gap" requires benchmarking LMs on human-scale datasets to understand how linguistic knowledge emerges from children's natural training data. Using transcripts from the BabyView dataset (videos from children ages 6-36 months), we investigate (1) scaling performance at child-scale data regimes, (2) variability in model performance across datasets from different children's experiences and linguistic predictors of dataset quality, and (3) relationships between model and child language learning outcomes. LMs trained on child data show acceptable scaling for grammar tasks, but lower scaling on semantic and world knowledge tasks than models trained on synthetic data; we also observe substantial variability on data from different children. Beyond dataset size, performance is most associated with a combination of distributional and interactional linguistic features, broadly consistent with what makes high-quality input for child language development. Finally, model likelihoods for individual words correlate with children's learning of those words, suggesting that properties of child-directed input may influence both model learning and human language development. Overall, understanding what properties make language data efficient for learning can enable more powerful small-scale language models while also shedding light on human language acquisition.

AI.tldr: LMs trained on child-scale natural language data show acceptable grammar scaling but poorer semantic/world knowledge scaling compared to synthetic data, with performance variability across children's experiences and correlations between model likelihoods and children's word learning.
AI.motivation: To understand the "data gap" between language models requiring massive training data versus human children learning from limited natural input, by benchmarking LMs on human-scale datasets to investigate how linguistic knowledge emerges from children's natural training data.
AI.method: Used transcripts from BabyView dataset (videos from children ages 6-36 months) to investigate: (1) scaling performance at child-scale data regimes, (2) variability across different children's experiences and linguistic predictors of dataset quality, and (3) relationships between model and child language learning outcomes.
AI.result: LMs trained on child data show acceptable scaling for grammar tasks but lower scaling on semantic and world knowledge tasks than models trained on synthetic data; substantial variability across different children's data; performance associated with combination of distributional and interactional linguistic features; model likelihoods for individual words correlate with children's learning of those words.
AI.conclusion: Understanding properties that make language data efficient for learning can enable more powerful small-scale language models while shedding light on human language acquisition, with child-directed input properties influencing both model learning and human language development.

title: M2H-MX: Multi-Task Dense Visual Perception for Real-Time Monocular Spatial Understanding
comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, 5 tables. Preprint under review
summary:
Monocular cameras are attractive for robotic perception due to their low cost and ease of deployment, yet achieving reliable real-time spatial understanding from a single image stream remains challenging. While recent multi-task dense prediction models have improved per-pixel depth and semantic estimation, translating these advances into stable monocular mapping systems is still non-trivial.
  This paper presents M2H-MX, a real-time multi-task perception model for monocular spatial understanding. The model preserves multi-scale feature representations while introducing register-gated global context and controlled cross-task interaction in a lightweight decoder, enabling depth and semantic predictions to reinforce each other under strict latency constraints. Its outputs integrate directly into an unmodified monocular SLAM pipeline through a compact perception-to-mapping interface.
  We evaluate both dense prediction accuracy and in-the-loop system performance. On NYUDv2, M2H-MX-L achieves state-of-the-art results, improving semantic mIoU by 6.6% and reducing depth RMSE by 9.4% over representative multi-task baselines. When deployed in a real-time monocular mapping system on ScanNet, M2H-MX reduces average trajectory error by 60.7% compared to a strong monocular SLAM baseline while producing cleaner metric-semantic maps. These results demonstrate that modern multi-task dense prediction can be reliably deployed for real-time monocular spatial perception in robotic systems.

AI.tldr: M2H-MX is a real-time multi-task perception model for monocular spatial understanding that improves depth and semantic predictions through register-gated global context and controlled cross-task interaction, enabling 60.7% reduction in trajectory error when integrated with monocular SLAM.
AI.motivation: Monocular cameras are attractive for robotic perception due to low cost and ease of deployment, but achieving reliable real-time spatial understanding from single image streams remains challenging. While multi-task dense prediction models have improved depth and semantic estimation, translating these advances into stable monocular mapping systems is non-trivial.
AI.method: M2H-MX preserves multi-scale feature representations while introducing register-gated global context and controlled cross-task interaction in a lightweight decoder. This enables depth and semantic predictions to reinforce each other under strict latency constraints. The model integrates directly into unmodified monocular SLAM pipelines through a compact perception-to-mapping interface.
AI.result: On NYUDv2, M2H-MX-L achieves state-of-the-art results: semantic mIoU improved by 6.6% and depth RMSE reduced by 9.4% over representative multi-task baselines. When deployed in real-time monocular mapping on ScanNet, M2H-MX reduces average trajectory error by 60.7% compared to strong monocular SLAM baseline while producing cleaner metric-semantic maps.
AI.conclusion: Modern multi-task dense prediction can be reliably deployed for real-time monocular spatial perception in robotic systems, demonstrating that improved dense prediction accuracy translates directly to enhanced system-level performance in monocular mapping applications.

title: LGFNet: Local-Global Fusion Network with Fidelity Gap Delta Learning for Multi-Source Aerodynamics
summary: The precise fusion of computational fluid dynamic (CFD) data, wind tunnel tests data, and flight tests data in aerodynamic area is essential for obtaining comprehensive knowledge of both localized flow structures and global aerodynamic trends across the entire flight envelope. However, existing methodologies often struggle to balance high-resolution local fidelity with wide-range global dependency, leading to either a loss of sharp discontinuities or an inability to capture long-range topological correlations. We propose Local-Global Fusion Network (LGFNet) for multi-scale feature decomposition to extract this dual-natured aerodynamic knowledge. To this end, LGFNet combines a spatial perception layer that integrates a sliding window mechanism with a relational reasoning layer based on self-attention, simultaneously reinforcing the continuity of fine-grained local features (e.g., shock waves) and capturing long-range flow information. Furthermore, the fidelity gap delta learning (FGDL) strategy is proposed to treat CFD data as a "low-frequency carrier" to explicitly approximate nonlinear discrepancies. This approach prevents unphysical smoothing while inheriting the foundational physical trends from the simulation baseline. Experiments demonstrate that LGFNet achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance in both accuracy and uncertainty reduction across diverse aerodynamic scenarios.

AI.tldr: LGFNet is a Local-Global Fusion Network that combines spatial perception with relational reasoning to extract multi-scale aerodynamic features from CFD, wind tunnel, and flight test data, using fidelity gap delta learning to preserve physical trends while capturing nonlinear discrepancies.
AI.motivation: Existing aerodynamic data fusion methods struggle to balance high-resolution local fidelity (e.g., shock waves) with wide-range global dependencies, often losing sharp discontinuities or failing to capture long-range topological correlations across the flight envelope.
AI.method: LGFNet combines: 1) spatial perception layer with sliding window mechanism for local feature extraction, 2) relational reasoning layer based on self-attention for capturing long-range flow information, and 3) fidelity gap delta learning (FGDL) strategy that treats CFD data as a "low-frequency carrier" to explicitly approximate nonlinear discrepancies while preserving physical trends.
AI.result: LGFNet achieves state-of-the-art performance in both accuracy and uncertainty reduction across diverse aerodynamic scenarios, demonstrating effective fusion of multi-source aerodynamic data while maintaining local discontinuities and global correlations.
AI.conclusion: The proposed LGFNet with FGDL strategy successfully addresses the local-global trade-off in aerodynamic data fusion, enabling comprehensive understanding of both localized flow structures and global aerodynamic trends across the entire flight envelope.

title: Can LLM Agents Identify Spoken Dialects like a Linguist?
summary: Due to the scarcity of labeled dialectal speech, audio dialect classification is a challenging task for most languages, including Swiss German. In this work, we explore the ability of large language models (LLMs) as agents in understanding the dialects and whether they can show comparable performance to models such as HuBERT in dialect classification. In addition, we provide an LLM baseline and a human linguist one. Our approach uses phonetic transcriptions produced by ASR systems and combines them with linguistic resources such as dialect feature maps, vowel history, and rules. Our findings indicate that, when linguistic information is provided, the LLM predictions improve. The human baseline shows that automatically generated transcriptions can be beneficial for such classifications, but also presents opportunities for improvement.

AI.tldr: LLMs with linguistic resources (phonetic transcriptions, dialect features, vowel history, rules) can approach HuBERT's performance in Swiss German dialect classification, though human linguist baseline reveals room for improvement in automatic transcriptions.
AI.motivation: Audio dialect classification is challenging due to scarce labeled dialectal speech, especially for Swiss German. The paper explores whether LLMs can understand dialects and achieve performance comparable to models like HuBERT, while establishing both LLM and human linguist baselines.
AI.method: Uses phonetic transcriptions from ASR systems combined with linguistic resources including dialect feature maps, vowel history, and rules. Compares LLM performance with HuBERT and establishes human linguist baseline to evaluate the utility of automatically generated transcriptions.
AI.result: LLM predictions improve when provided with linguistic information, approaching HuBERT's performance. Human baseline shows that automatically generated transcriptions can be beneficial for dialect classification but also reveals opportunities for improvement in transcription quality.
AI.conclusion: LLMs with appropriate linguistic resources can be effective for dialect classification, though automatic transcriptions need refinement. The approach demonstrates the value of combining ASR outputs with linguistic knowledge for low-resource dialect analysis tasks.

title: Diffusion Mental Averages
summary: Can a diffusion model produce its own "mental average" of a concept-one that is as sharp and realistic as a typical sample? We introduce Diffusion Mental Averages (DMA), a model-centric answer to this question. While prior methods aim to average image collections, they produce blurry results when applied to diffusion samples from the same prompt. These data-centric techniques operate outside the model, ignoring the generative process. In contrast, DMA averages within the diffusion model's semantic space, as discovered by recent studies. Since this space evolves across timesteps and lacks a direct decoder, we cast averaging as trajectory alignment: optimize multiple noise latents so their denoising trajectories progressively converge toward shared coarse-to-fine semantics, yielding a single sharp prototype. We extend our approach to multimodal concepts (e.g., dogs with many breeds) by clustering samples in semantically-rich spaces such as CLIP and applying Textual Inversion or LoRA to bridge CLIP clusters into diffusion space. This is, to our knowledge, the first approach that delivers consistent, realistic averages, even for abstract concepts, serving as a concrete visual summary and a lens into model biases and concept representation.

AI.tldr: Diffusion Mental Averages (DMA) enables diffusion models to generate sharp, realistic "mental averages" of concepts by averaging within the model's semantic space through trajectory alignment, rather than blurry image averaging.
AI.motivation: Prior methods for averaging image collections produce blurry results when applied to diffusion samples, as they operate outside the model and ignore the generative process. The authors aim to enable diffusion models to produce their own sharp, realistic concept averages.
AI.method: DMA averages within the diffusion model's semantic space by optimizing multiple noise latents so their denoising trajectories progressively converge toward shared coarse-to-fine semantics, yielding a single sharp prototype. For multimodal concepts, samples are clustered in semantically-rich spaces like CLIP, then bridged into diffusion space using Textual Inversion or LoRA.
AI.result: DMA delivers consistent, realistic averages even for abstract concepts, producing sharp prototypes that serve as visual summaries and provide insights into model biases and concept representation.
AI.conclusion: DMA represents the first approach to produce consistent, realistic concept averages from diffusion models by working within the model's semantic space rather than averaging images externally, offering both practical visual summaries and analytical insights into model behavior.

title: Deep Learning-Based Anomaly Detection in Spacecraft Telemetry on Edge Devices
comment: IEEE Space Computing Conference (SCC 2025), Los Angeles, CA, USA, 28 July - 1 August 2025
summary: Spacecraft anomaly detection is critical for mission safety, yet deploying sophisticated models on-board presents significant challenges due to hardware constraints. This paper investigates three approaches for spacecraft telemetry anomaly detection -- forecasting & threshold, direct classification, and image classification -- and optimizes them for edge deployment using multi-objective neural architecture optimization on the European Space Agency Anomaly Dataset. Our baseline experiments demonstrate that forecasting & threshold achieves superior detection performance (92.7% Corrected Event-wise F0.5-score (CEF0.5)) [1] compared to alternatives. Through Pareto-optimal architecture optimization, we dramatically reduced computational requirements while maintaining capabilities -- the optimized forecasting & threshold model preserved 88.8% CEF0.5 while reducing RAM usage by 97.1% to just 59 KB and operations by 99.4%. Analysis of deployment viability shows our optimized models require just 0.36-6.25% of CubeSat RAM, making on-board anomaly detection practical even on highly constrained hardware. This research demonstrates that sophisticated anomaly detection capabilities can be successfully deployed within spacecraft edge computing constraints, providing near-instantaneous detection without exceeding hardware limitations or compromising mission safety.

AI.tldr: Multi-objective neural architecture optimization enables deployment of spacecraft anomaly detection models on highly constrained edge hardware, achieving 97.1% RAM reduction while maintaining 88.8% detection performance.
AI.motivation: Spacecraft anomaly detection is critical for mission safety, but deploying sophisticated models on-board is challenging due to hardware constraints of spacecraft edge computing platforms.
AI.method: Investigated three anomaly detection approaches (forecasting & threshold, direct classification, image classification) and optimized them using multi-objective neural architecture optimization on the European Space Agency Anomaly Dataset.
AI.result: Forecasting & threshold achieved best performance (92.7% CEF0.5). Optimized model preserved 88.8% CEF0.5 while reducing RAM by 97.1% to 59 KB and operations by 99.4%, requiring only 0.36-6.25% of CubeSat RAM.
